newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi Sec denies reported "tobashi" deals.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi Sec denies reported "tobashi" deals.

text.p: Japan's Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd on Friday denied a newspaper report that it had conducted questionable "tobashi" deals in securities.

"We have not found any such transactions," Yamaichi said in a statement, referring to Friday's report by the daily Sankei Shimbun that said the brokerage had engaged in questionable "tobashi" transactions in securities with Tokyu Department Store Co Ltd between 1987 and 1992.

In "tobashi" or "pitching" transactions, brokerages shift investment losses suffered by one client to another firm, typically one with a different financial year, to prevent a favoured client from having to report the loss. Such deals could be determined to be violation of Japan's securities law.

"We will investigate the case, which might be deals between clients. At present, we have not found any violation of Japanese regulations such as a guarantee of returns to Tokyu Department store," said Yamaichi, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages.
A Tokyu spokesman said the firm was looking into the allegations and the result of the inquiry was not yet available.
